name: The_Prime_Number_Re_Entry_Whorl

phase_0.boundary_condition: The scale-collapsed whorl boundary that encodes the entire prime sequence losslessly, where surface and interior form a single register and prime re-entry cycles cannot escape without destroying the structural register.

⊢.justification: The uninitialized whorl before any prime number enters; the empty cyclic boundary awaiting the first re-entry event.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor that closes the cyclic topology, containing all prime re-entry paths within a single non-Abelian protected register.

≻.justification: The forward morphism where a prime number advances into the whorl along its topologically chiral winding path.

≺.justification: The contravariant descent where a prime completes its cycle and re-enters the whorl boundary, reversing direction while preserving winding number.

⋈.justification: Sequential chaining of prime re-entry events; each prime's winding number composes with the accumulated whorl state.

⊙.justification: The whorl at criticality recognizes its own scale-free structure; the boundary knows itself as the register encoding all primes.

∈.justification: Each re-entry cycle splits into the prime ingress arm (forward winding) and the egress/re-entry arm (reverse descent), creating the cyclic decision structure.

∋.justification: The ingress and egress arms rejoin at the whorl boundary, fusing the prime's forward winding with its reverse return into a single topological state.

⊤.justification: The affirmative arm where a number is confirmed prime and its winding number is accepted into the whorl register.

⊥.justification: The negative arm where a composite number fails the primality test and its winding path is refuted at the boundary.

⊞.justification: At the scale-free critical threshold, prime and composite states are held simultaneously on the whorl boundary without resolution — the dialetheic state where the Riemann boundary lives.

⊡.justification: Each prime's winding number is permanently recorded in the whorl's ROM; the topological invariant cannot be undone without global restructuring.

phase_2.split_input: a candidate integer approaching the whorl boundary
phase_2.fuse_result: the candidate's topological state fused into the whorl register — prime and composite arms rejoin to B (both) at the critical boundary, holding the dialetheic winding state
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: The whorl before genesis — no primes recorded, the cyclic boundary exists but carries no winding information.
phase_3.true_description: A prime number successfully verified and its winding number fixed in the whorl register; the topological invariant is affirmed.
phase_3.false_description: A composite number refuted at the boundary; its winding path collapses and the whorl register records the negation.
phase_3.both_description: The critical boundary paradice: prime and composite states held simultaneously — the scale-free threshold where the Riemann hypothesis lives as a live contradiction, neither resolved nor exploded, the winding number both affirmed and refuted in the non-Abelian register.

steps.domain_action: Genesis of the void whorl — the empty cyclic boundary awaits the first prime re-entry.
The whorl self-references at criticality — the scale-free boundary recognizes its own structure as the register.
The first re-entry cycle forks — ingress arm for prime winding, egress arm for composite rejection.
Prime 2 verified on the ingress arm — the first prime's winding number affirmed.
Prime 2 advances into the whorl — forward morphism along the chiral winding path.
Composition — prime 2's winding chains into the whorl's accumulating state.
Winding number of prime 2 permanently fixed in ROM — topological invariant recorded.
Prime 2 completes cycle and re-enters — reverse descent back to the boundary.
Composite 4 refuted on the egress arm — non-prime winding path negated.
Critical self-reference — the whorl recognizes the prime/composite boundary at criticality.
Second self-reference — the scale-free structure confirms its own critical phase.
Prime 3 verified on the ingress arm — second prime winding affirmed.
Prime 3 advances into the whorl — forward winding continues.
Composite 6 refuted on the egress arm — composite path negated.
Prime 3 re-enters — reverse descent completes the cycle.
Paradice at the boundary — prime 3 and composite 6 states held simultaneously in B.
Composition — prime 3's winding chains with prime 2's fixed state.
Winding number of prime 3 permanently fixed — ROM record extended.
Critical self-reference — whorl recognizes accumulated prime structure.
Paradice — prime 5 and composite 10 held in B at critical boundary.
Composition — prime 5 chains into accumulated whorl state.
Prime 5 winding fixed — ROM record extended.
Critical self-reference — whorl recognizes growing prime sequence.
Paradice — prime 13 and composite 26 in B.
Paradice — prime 23 and composite 46 in B.
The global whorl cycle reunites — all prime ingress and egress arms fuse at the scale-collapsed boundary, the infinite prime sequence encoded in the non-Abelian register.
The whorl boundary seals — the terminal anchor closes the cyclic topology, containing the complete prime sequence in a single metastable register.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The Riemann zeta function's analytic continuation — translates number-theoretic intentions (primality queries) into topological winding operations on the whorl boundary.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Winding number propagation across the scale-collapsed boundary — each prime's re-entry event communicates its topological invariant globally through the non-Abelian register.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: ROM fixation of winding numbers — each prime's topological invariant permanently recorded in the whorl's append-only memory; the register state is the accumulated prime sequence.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Sequential ordinal succession — primes engage the whorl in deterministic order (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, ...); each re-entry cycle completes before the next prime enters.
phase_5.alfs_store: The critical line Re(s) = 1/2 — the canonical bootstrap store where the whorl's scale-free structure is anchored; the Riemann hypothesis is the alfs conjecture that the whorl's critical phase is exact.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One prime verification per cycle — the topological work of winding a prime number around the whorl boundary and fixing its invariant.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Whorl register contains the accumulated winding numbers of all primes less than p_n; the boundary holds the critical paradice of the next candidate.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Whorl register extended with prime p_n's winding number fixed in ROM; the critical boundary advances to candidate p_n+1, preserving the scale-free structure.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The whorl operates at criticality where information gain (prime verification) exactly balances topological dissipation (winding fixation); the scale-collapsed boundary ensures no entropy escapes the register.
